segments.text: You just need the key information.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst nid ðə ki ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: Also, did you notice that Jason repeated the location and Anne checked it back with him?
segments.ipa: /ˈɔlsoʊ dɪd ju ˈnoʊtəs ðæt ˈdʒeɪsən rɪˈpitɪd ðə loʊˈkeɪʃən ənd æn tʃɛkt ɪt bæk wɪð hɪm/

segments.text: Miller Road near the gas station before the bridge.

segments.text: Is that correct?
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðæt kərˈɛkt/

segments.text: That's a great habit because if the address is wrong, help goes to the wrong place.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ɡreɪt ˈhæbət bɪˈkɔz ɪf ðə ˈæˌdrɛs ɪz rɔŋ hɛlp ɡoʊz tu ðə rɔŋ pleɪs/

segments.text: And now the most important point of this conversation.
segments.ipa: /ənd naʊ ðə moʊst ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt pɔɪnt ʌv ðɪs ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən/

segments.text: Max, tell them.
segments.ipa: /mæks tɛl ðɛm/

segments.text: Okay, listen carefully because this one could really matter.
segments.ipa: /ˌoʊˈkeɪ ˈlɪsən ˈkɛrfəli bɪˈkɔz ðɪs wʌn kʊd ˈrɪli ˈmætər/

segments.text: If someone has been in an accident, do not move them.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsʌmˌwʌn hæz bɪn ɪn æn ˈæksədənt du nɑt muv ðɛm/

segments.text: Seriously, moving a person after a crash can make their injuries much worse, especially the neck and the back.
segments.ipa: /ˈsɪriəsli ˈmuvɪŋ ə ˈpɝsən ˈæftər ə kræʃ kæn meɪk ðɛr ˈɪndʒəriz mʌtʃ wɝs əˈspɛʃli ðə nɛk ənd ðə bæk/

segments.text: It can even cause permanent damage.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn ˈivɪn kɑz ˈpɝmənənt ˈdæmədʒ/

segments.text: And that's why Anne told Jason to stay with her, talk to her, and keep her calm,
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæts waɪ æn toʊld ˈdʒeɪsən tu steɪ wɪð hɝ tɔk tu hɝ ənd kip hɝ kɑm/

segments.text: but not to move her.
segments.ipa: /bʌt nɑt tu muv hɝ/

segments.text: The experts, the paramedics know how to do it safely.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɛkspərts ðə ˌpɛrəˈmɛdɪks noʊ haʊ tu du ɪt ˈseɪfli/

segments.text: So, the best thing you can do is wait for them.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə bɛst θɪŋ ju kæn du ɪz weɪt fɔr ðɛm/

segments.text: The only exception is if it's a matter of life or death.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈoʊnli ɪkˈsɛpʃən ɪz ɪf ɪts ə ˈmætər ʌv laɪf ɔr dɛθ/

segments.text: For example, if there's fire, if the car is about to explode, or if the person is in immediate danger.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ðɛrz ˈfaɪər ɪf ðə kɑr ɪz əˈbaʊt tu ɪkˈsploʊd ɔr ɪf ðə ˈpɝsən ɪz ɪn ˌɪˈmiˌdiət ˈdeɪndʒər/

segments.text: In that case, you have to get them out.
segments.ipa: /ɪn ðæt keɪs ju hæv tu ɡɛt ðɛm aʊt/

segments.text: But if there's no immediate danger, don't touch them. Remember that.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ðɛrz noʊ ˌɪˈmiˌdiət ˈdeɪndʒər doʊnt tʌtʃ ðɛm rɪˈmɛmbər ðæt/

segments.text: It's one of the most useful things you can take from today's episode. All right.
segments.ipa: /ɪts wʌn ʌv ðə moʊst ˈjusfəl θɪŋz ju kæn teɪk frʌm təˈdeɪz ˈɛpəˌsoʊd ɔl raɪt/

segments.text: Now, let's move on to a different kind of emergency. Yes.
segments.ipa: /naʊ lɛts muv ɑn tu ə ˈdɪfərənt kaɪnd ʌv ɪˈmɝdʒənsi jɛs/

segments.text: And this one is a bit harder.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɪs wʌn ɪz ə bɪt ˈhɑrdər/

segments.text: It's sad, but it's something that could happen to any of us.
segments.ipa: /ɪts sæd bʌt ɪts ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt kʊd ˈhæpən tu ˈɛni ʌv ʌs/

segments.text: Imagine you're at home and suddenly you hear screaming coming from the apartment next door.
segments.ipa: /ˌɪˈmædʒən jʊr æt hoʊm ənd ˈsʌdənli ju hir ˈskrimɪŋ ˈkʌmɪŋ frʌm ðə əˈpɑrtmənt nɛkst dɔr/

segments.text: Maybe you hear something break or a voice yelling for help and you think someone might be getting attacked.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju hir ˈsʌmθɪŋ breɪk ɔr ə vɔɪs ˈjɛlɪŋ fɔr hɛlp ənd ju θɪŋk ˈsʌmˌwʌn maɪt bi ˈɡɛtɪŋ əˈtækt/

segments.text: In a situation like this, it's not your job to go in and solve it.
segments.ipa: /ɪn ə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən laɪk ðɪs ɪts nɑt jɔr dʒɑb tu ɡoʊ ɪn ənd sɑlv ɪt/

segments.text: Your job is to call for help and to explain clearly what you heard so the police can act.
segments.ipa: /jɔr dʒɑb ɪz tu kɔl fɔr hɛlp ənd tu ɪkˈspleɪn ˈklɪrli wʌt ju hɝd soʊ ðə pəˈlis kæn ækt/

segments.text: And that's what we'll practice today.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæts wʌt wil ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: How to describe sounds, explain what you heard, and say if you think someone is in danger.
segments.ipa: /haʊ tu dɪˈskraɪb saʊndz ɪkˈspleɪn wʌt ju hɝd ənd seɪ ɪf ju θɪŋk ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɪz ɪn ˈdeɪndʒər/

segments.text: Let's look at five useful expressions for this situation.
segments.ipa: /lɛts lʊk æt faɪv ˈjusfəl ɪkˈsprɛʃənz fɔr ðɪs ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: Number one, I can hear screaming or I heard screaming.
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌmbər wʌn aɪ kæn hir ˈskrimɪŋ ɔr aɪ hɝd ˈskrimɪŋ/

segments.text: Use I can hear when it's happening right now and I heard when it already happened.
segments.ipa: /jus aɪ kæn hir wɛn ɪts ˈhæpənɪŋ raɪt naʊ ənd aɪ hɝd wɛn ɪt ɔlˈrɛdi ˈhæpənd/

segments.text: For example, I can hear screaming coming from the apartment next door.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl aɪ kæn hir ˈskrimɪŋ ˈkʌmɪŋ frʌm ðə əˈpɑrtmənt nɛkst dɔr/

segments.text: Number two, it sounds like this is perfect when you're not sure what's happening,
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌmbər tu ɪt saʊndz laɪk ðɪs ɪz pərˈfɛkt wɛn jʊr nɑt ʃʊr wʌts ˈhæpənɪŋ/

segments.text: but you want to describe what you think.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju wɑnt tu dɪˈskraɪb wʌt ju θɪŋk/

segments.ipa: /laɪk ɪt saʊndz laɪk ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɪz ˈbiɪŋ əˈtækt ɔr ɪt saʊndz laɪk ə mæn ənd ə ˈwʊmən ɑr ˈfaɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: You're not saying you're 100% sure.
segments.ipa: /jʊr nɑt ˈseɪɪŋ jʊr ʃʊr/

segments.text: You're describing what it sounds like.
segments.ipa: /jʊr dɪˈskraɪbɪŋ wʌt ɪt saʊndz laɪk/

segments.text: Number three, I think someone is in danger.
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌmbər θri aɪ θɪŋk ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɪz ɪn ˈdeɪndʒər/

segments.text: Or I'm afraid someone is going to get hurt.

segments.text: This is how you tell the operator why you're calling.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz haʊ ju tɛl ðə ˈɑpərˌeɪtər waɪ jʊr ˈkɔlɪŋ/

segments.text: I think someone is in danger.
segments.ipa: /aɪ θɪŋk ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɪz ɪn ˈdeɪndʒər/

segments.text: I heard a woman yelling for help.
segments.ipa: /aɪ hɝd ə ˈwʊmən ˈjɛlɪŋ fɔr hɛlp/

segments.text: Number four, it's coming from.
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌmbər fɔr ɪts ˈkʌmɪŋ frʌm/

segments.text: This helps you say where the sound is coming from.

segments.text: The noise is coming from apartment 4B right next to mine.
segments.ipa: /ðə nɔɪz ɪz ˈkʌmɪŋ frʌm əˈpɑrtmənt bi raɪt nɛkst tu maɪn/

segments.text: Or it's coming from the apartment upstairs.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ɪts ˈkʌmɪŋ frʌm ðə əˈpɑrtmənt əpˈstɛrz/

segments.text: That helps the police know exactly where to go.
segments.ipa: /ðæt hɛlps ðə pəˈlis noʊ ɪɡˈzæktli wɛr tu ɡoʊ/

segments.text: And number five, it started about minutes ago or it's been going on for time matters.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈnʌmbər faɪv ɪt ˈstɑrtɪd əˈbaʊt ˈmɪnəts əˈɡoʊ ɔr ɪts bɪn ˈɡoʊɪŋ ɑn fɔr taɪm ˈmætərz/

segments.text: It started about 5 minutes ago or it's been going on for almost 10 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈstɑrtɪd əˈbaʊt ˈmɪnəts əˈɡoʊ ɔr ɪts bɪn ˈɡoʊɪŋ ɑn fɔr ˈɔlˌmoʊst ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: The operator will use that to decide how urgent it is.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɑpərˌeɪtər wɪl jus ðæt tu ˌdɪˈsaɪd haʊ ˈɝdʒənt ɪt ɪz/
